newsitem.title: UK: Hambros merges fund business with Guinness Flight.
newsitem.headline: Hambros merges fund business with Guinness Flight.

text.p: Hambros Plc said on Sunday it will merge its Hambros Fund Management (HFM) unit with Guinness Flight Global Asset Management -- a move bringing combined funds under management to 9.3 billion sterling.
Hambros will exchange shares in HFM for the issue of new shares in Guinness Flight, as well as acquiring further shares, to form Guinness Flight Hambro Asset Management, Hambros said in a statement.

The merger of the two Britain-based firms will give the new company greater financial strength, an enhanced product range in three key areas of managed currency funds, Asian equity funds, and cash and fixed interest management, and increased offshore fund assets, Hambros said.
"This is an excellent move for HFM and all its clients," said Andrew Martin Smith, HFM's managing director.
"We are two highly complementary firms and I know that, together, we will be able to deliver an enhanced level of service."

Hambros said substantial cost savings would be made through the cutting of marketing, pricing and administration costs in shareholder services and through combined central operational functions such as accounting and personnel.

"Guinness Flight Hambro will see a significant increase in the size of funds under management in all of its principal areas of business, thereby enjoying the benefits of increased economies of scale in each of these business segments," it added.
On completion of the deal, Guinness Mahon Holdings Plc and Hambros will each hold a 42.5 percent stake in the new firm, with around 15.0 percent held by management.
But Hambros added that options schemes could push management's stake up to 30 percent when appropriate targets are met.

Tim Guinness, currently joint managing director of Guinness Flight, will become chief executive of Guinness Flight Hambro, while HFM's Smith will become deputy chief executive of the new firm. The deputy chariman's position will be take up by Howard Flight, currently joint managing director of Guinness Flight.
